title: MeshBench: streaming-aware attention scheduling and golden stability harness
creator: Lin Chen
description: Create MeshBench: a next-generation benchmarking harness that measures runtime interactions between kernel selection, attention-window optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling under streaming workloads. The harness will produce reproducible 'golden stability' baselines (seeded KV/cache state + deterministic sampler), a micro-synth traffic generator for streaming/pipelined requests, and CI perf gate integrations that validate quantile stability and regression deltas for both single-request latency and batched throughput.
acceptance_criteria: MeshBench can replay a representative streaming workload (mix of short/long, many-tool calls, and streaming tokens) with seeded KV cache state reproducibly across 95% of runs.
We add 6 canonical baseline profiles (short-chat, long-prefill, multimodel-fanout, tool-heavy, bursty-batched, tail-latency-stressed) with golden metrics checked into a lockfile.

CI performance gate added: 99th percentile latency regression threshold configurable per-profile and integrated with PR checks; PRs exceeding threshold must auto-fail and attach a regression artifact.
End-to-end dashboard visuals (throughput vs. latency heatmaps, kernel selection frequency matrix, attention-window hit-rate) available in Console staging for stakeholders.
Documentation + runbook for adding new profiles and for interpreting golden-diff artifacts delivered (Confluence doc & sample GH action).
plan: Design: finalize canonical profiles and required telemetry (kernel id, attention window, kv-hit, batch size, scheduling trace).
Engine: implement streaming traffic generator with determinism knobs (seeded RNG, fixed inter-arrival distributions, KV cache seeding).
Bench: integrate kernel-probe hooks to record selected kernel variants per timestep and capture attention optimization flags.
Stabilize: iterate to reduce run-to-run variance (noise injection control, warmup warm-cache protocol, cgroup pinning for CPU/GPU).
CI: add GH action to run lightweight golden check on PR with baseline comparison and artifact upload for failing regressions.
Docs: write runbook and onboarding guide for platform/eng to add new profiles and interpret diffs.
milestones: M3 - Kernel and attention probes integrated (2026-03-30)
M4 - Golden baseline lockfile & CI action (2026-04-06)
measurements: Run-to-run standard deviation on 99th percentile latency < 3% for short-chat profile after stabilization.
KV-cache hit-rate reproducibility within +/- 1 percentage point across seeded runs.
Kernel-selection distribution drift measured as JS divergence < 0.02 vs golden for non-regression runs.
CI gate false-positive rate < 2% over a two-week window after calibration.
risks: High environmental noise on shared CI runners causing flaky baselines (mitigation: use reserved infra or docker cgroups + warmup).
Determinism limits for models with nondeterministic ops or FP16 rounding differences across kernels (mitigation: capture per-kernel tolerance and separate numeric-sensitivity profiles).
Large storage cost for golden artifacts and trace captures (mitigation: sample-level artifacts + retention policy).
notes: Goal is to measure interaction effects — e.g., how kernel routing decisions change when streaming prefill and decode overlap versus isolated runs.
We should keep golden baselines intentionally tied to runtime-1.22 kernel selection defaults and tag lockfile with runtime/commit hash.
Consider adding a small 'chaos' mode later that fuzzes inter-arrival times to simulate burst mixing.
